cover.title: The bond market just hit a 24-year high

slides.label: Treasury yields
slides.body: The government borrows by selling bonds, and the yield is the interest it pays. The 10-year yield is the benchmark for mortgages, student loans and credit cards.

slides.label: How high it went
slides.body: The US 30-year yield hit 5.59% on Sept 29, the highest since 2002. The 10-year topped 5.3% in October. The UK 30-year gilt passed 6% on Oct 1.

visual.footnote: BAR LENGTH = YIELD LEVEL AT PEAK

slides.label: Why it happened
slides.body: Oil spiked on Iran-related supply fears, with Brent above $100. Inflation worries grew, the Fed kept raising rates, and bond prices fell, pushing yields up.

visual.caption: OIL UP · INFLATION FEARS UP · YIELDS UP

slides.label: This week
slides.body: The 10-year yield slid below 5% as a tech selloff sent money into Treasuries. But the NY Fed's Williams says sticky inflation still points to tighter policy.
slides.source: Sources: Federal Reserve H.15, Nuveen, Wisevoter (Nov 24)

caption:
The bond market just hit its highest yields in 24 years. 📈

The US 30-year hit 5.59% on Sept 29, the highest since 2002. The 10-year topped 5.3% in October. This week it slid back below 5% as a tech selloff pushed money into Treasuries.

Why it matters: the 10-year yield sets the tone for mortgages, student loans and credit cards.
